standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-coherent module over a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is the filtered union of its finite type quasi-coherent submodules, cited from the properties chapter

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite type module over a quasi-compact scheme is generated by finitely many sections over each member of a finite affine cover
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the sections g over the members of a finite affine cover of the given open that have to lie in the submodule.

core_obligations: Collect the data to be controlled: take the graded ideal constructed for the closed subscheme and the auxiliary local data attached to it, and note that outside the image of the closed subscheme the d-th piece of the graded algebra agrees with the ideal already in degree d, so the open in question lies in the locus where nothing has to be cut out (proof lines 8164-8173).

Make the data finite: cover the given quasi-compact open by finitely many affine opens, generate the d-th piece of the graded algebra over each of them by finitely many sections, and apply the finite type submodule statement to a quasi-coherent module over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base to obtain a finite type submodule of the d-th piece of the ideal containing all the auxiliary local sections and all the chosen generators (proof lines 8174-8183).

Conclude: the resulting finite type submodule is a solution, because by construction both the defining condition for the closed subscheme and the disjointness of the support from the given open are satisfied (proof lines 8184-8187).
proof_roadmap: Reuse the construction of the graded ideal for the closed subscheme and observe that the given open avoids everything that has to be cut out (proof lines 8164-8173).
Reduce to finitely many local sections and pick a finite type submodule containing them all, which is then the required solution (proof lines 8174-8187).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a quasi-compact quasi-separated base with a graded algebra whose pieces are finite type, a closed subscheme of finite presentation of the relative Proj that avoids the image of a quasi-compact open is the relative Proj of the graded quotient by a finite type submodule of one graded piece, chosen so that its support misses that open (statement lines 8144-8162). The counted proof is a finiteness argument: it reuses the graded ideal constructed earlier for the closed subscheme, notes that over the given open nothing has to be cut out, covers that open by finitely many affines, generates the relevant graded piece over them by finitely many sections, and then uses that a quasi-coherent module over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base is the filtered union of its finite type submodules to find one finite type submodule containing all the sections that have to be controlled (proof lines 8164-8187). It is H2: the argument is short and completely carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the earlier construction and the finite type submodule statement.
